title: Does steering a vision-language model's safety concept work through the text or the image pathway?

original_idea.body: Extract a refusal vector from text-only contrasts in an open VLM, test whether it steers refusal for text vs image-grounded prompts, and isolate whether image inputs evade the text-derived steering.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: whether text-built safety directions cover image-grounded jailbreaks targets a growing surface.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: VLM refusal vector across text vs image; VLM internals add friction.

low_compute.reasoning: Small VLM inference on one GPU.

novelty.reasoning: VLM steering emerging; pathway-isolation framing may be partly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Image-pathway evasion question may be open.
